title: Five-class provenance of chatbot text in student writing and programming (FLoRA, RelianceScope): code, analysis plans, statistics
description: Version 1.4.0. Code, time-stamped analysis plans and statistics files for a study of verbatim uptake of chatbot text in students' graded project proposals (FLoRA Open Data IPS, 275 students). v1.1.0 added plan R1: time-aware echo correction, third-source filter, clock check from chat-box keystrokes, validation against logged paste events, and extended analyses of grades and detection. v1.2.0 adds plan R2: three open zero-shot AI-text detectors (log-likelihood, Fast-DetectGPT, Binoculars on Qwen2.5 models) evaluated against logged provenance at paragraph level, by first language, and sensitivity of the third-source threshold. All analyses are exploratory. No third-party data are redistributed. v1.3.0 adds plan R3: attribution of each token of the submitted artefact to five provenance classes (chatbot-first, echo, shared source, typed, untraced insertion), applied to FLoRA and to the RelianceScope programming dataset with validation against human response-use codes and an unaided post-test; FLoRA detector reanalysis on typed vs untraced text (post hoc). Third-party data are not redistributed. v1.4.0 adds plan R4: entry mode by edit size, validation of typed and untraced classes against logged pastes, chance baseline and conservative bounds for chatbot-first code, length-controlled validation against human codes, and a censored model of the post-test.
